info.title: Actions HTTP Endpoint
info.description:
The Actions API is a higher-level alternative to the Mutations API. It is normally used by Studio in the course of regular authoring workflows, but can also be used directly if you wish. All requests have to be authenticated.

This API allows you to perform various operations on documents, versions, and releases in your Sanity dataset. Each request can contain multiple actions that will be executed in a single transaction.

Document Actions:
* `sanity.action.document.create`: Creates a new document in the dataset.
* `sanity.action.document.delete`: Deletes a document from the dataset.
* `sanity.action.document.edit`: Modifies an existing document using a patch.
* `sanity.action.document.publish`: Publishes a document, making it available in the published perspective.
* `sanity.action.document.unpublish`: Unpublishes a document, removing it from the published perspective.
* `sanity.action.document.discard`: [DEPRECATED] Discards a document (use version actions instead)
* `sanity.action.document.replaceDraft`: [DEPRECATED] Replaces a draft document (use version actions instead)

Version Actions:
* `sanity.action.document.version.create`: Creates a new version of a document in a release.
* `sanity.action.document.version.discard`: Discards a version of a document, optionally purging its history.
* `sanity.action.document.version.replace`: Replaces an existing version of a document.
* `sanity.action.document.version.unpublish`: Marks a version for unpublishing when the release is published.

Release Actions:
* `sanity.action.release.create`: Creates a new release with optional metadata.
* `sanity.action.release.edit`: Modifies the metadata of an existing release.
* `sanity.action.release.publish`: Publishes all documents in a release.
* `sanity.action.release.archive`: Archives a release, removing it from active releases.
* `sanity.action.release.unarchive`: Restores an archived release to its pre-archived state.
* `sanity.action.release.schedule`: Schedules a release for publishing at a future time.
* `sanity.action.release.unschedule`: Cancels a scheduled release.
* `sanity.action.release.delete`: Deletes a published or archived release.
* `sanity.action.release.import`: Imports a release document.

Note that it is not permitted to mix different types of actions, such as release and document actions, in a single API call.

API version requirements:
* The Actions API is available from API version `v2024-05-23`. Earlier versions return `404 Not Found`.
* Version and release actions, and `versions.<release>.` document IDs, require API version `v2025-02-19` or later. On earlier versions, release actions return `400 Bad Request` and document IDs must use the `drafts.` prefix.

Every action rejects fields it doesn't recognize with a `400 Bad Request` error, so field names must match this reference exactly.

servers.description: Parameterized base URL for Sanity API endpoints

projectId.description: Your Sanity project ID. This can be found in your project settings or in the URL when accessing your project in the Sanity management interface.

apiVersion.description: The version of the API to use. This should match the version specified in the info.version field.

parameters.name: dataset
parameters.description: The dataset to perform actions on. This is the name of your Sanity dataset.

post.description:
Execute one or more actions in a single transaction. Each action must specify its type and required parameters.
All actions must be valid and you must have permission to perform them.

The actions are executed in the order they appear in the request. If any action fails, the entire transaction is rolled back.

Important notes:
- You cannot mix different types of actions (e.g., release and document actions) in a single API call
- Documents in a release that isn't `active` (for example, while it's scheduled or publishing) are locked and cannot be modified
- Release IDs can't match an existing release, including published and archived releases; an ID becomes available again once its release is deleted
- Documents remain in retention after archiving and can be accessed via the document history endpoint

createDocument.description: Demonstrates how to create a new document of type "post" with a specific ID using the document create action.

deleteDocument.description: Shows how to delete a document by its published ID, including any associated drafts or version documents.

editDocument.description: Demonstrates editing an existing document by applying a patch to a specific version.

publishDocument.description: Publishes a specific version of a document, replacing the published document with its content.

unpublishDocument.description: Unpublishes a document by deleting the published document, keeping its content in the given draft or version.

createVersionFromDocument.summary: Create a version from a document
createVersionFromDocument.description: Creates a new version of a document in a release by providing the full document object.

createVersionFromExisting.summary: Create a version by copying from an existing document
createVersionFromExisting.description: Creates a new version by copying attributes from an existing document, optionally checking a base revision ID.

discardVersion.description: Discards a specific version of a document, optionally purging its history from the dataset.

replaceVersion.description: Replaces an existing version of a document with a new document object, updating its content.

unpublishVersion.description: Marks a version for unpublishing so that when the release is published, the published document will be removed.

createRelease.description: Demonstrates how to create a new release with metadata, such as a title, using the release create action.

editRelease.description: Shows how to edit the metadata of an existing release using a patch operation.

publishRelease.description: Publishes all documents in a release, replacing the published documents with the release content.

archiveRelease.description: Archives a release, removing it from active releases but retaining its documents in retention.

unarchiveRelease.description: Restores an archived release to its pre-archived state, making it active again.

scheduleRelease.description: Schedules a release to be published at a specific future time, locking the release until then.

unscheduleRelease.description: Cancels a previously scheduled release, unlocking it for further edits.

deleteRelease.description: Deletes a published or archived release from the dataset, removing its backing system document.

multipleActions.summary: Dispatch multiple actions in a single request
multipleActions.description:
Demonstrates how to dispatch multiple actions in a single transaction. In this example, a document is edited and then published in the same request.
Note that it is not permitted to mix different types of actions, such as release and document actions, in a single transaction.

discardDocument.description: [DEPRECATED] Discards a draft version of a document. Use version actions instead.

replaceDraftDocument.description: [DEPRECATED] Replaces a draft document with new content. Use version actions instead.

200.description: The actions were successfully executed in a single transaction. Any warnings are returned in `X-Sanity-Warning` response headers.

400.description:
The request was invalid. This could be due to:
- Missing required fields, or fields the action doesn't recognize
- Invalid action types
- Invalid parameters for actions
- Invalid document IDs or types
- Mixing different types of actions in a single request
- Release actions sent with an API version earlier than `v2025-02-19`
- A release that doesn't exist, or isn't in a state that allows the action (for example, publishing a scheduled release)
- Modifying documents in a release that is locked because it's scheduled or publishing
- Deleting a release that still contains documents

401.description: The request was not authenticated. Make sure you're using a valid API token.

403.description: The request was not authorized. Your API token doesn't have permission to perform the requested actions.

404.description:
A document the action needs doesn't exist, such as the draft or version being published or discarded, or the published document being unpublished.
The whole endpoint also returns `404 Not Found` for API versions earlier than `v2024-05-23`.

409.description:
The request conflicts with the current state of the dataset. This could be due to:
- Creating a document or release that already exists
- A revision check (such as `ifVersionRevisionId`, `ifPublishedRevisionId`, `ifBaseRevisionId`, or `ifRevisionID`) that doesn't match the current revision
- Deleting a published document while a draft or version exists that isn't listed in `includeDrafts`
- Reusing a `transactionId`

500.description: An internal server error occurred. This is usually temporary and the request can be retried.

BearerAuth.description: Authentication using a Bearer token. The token should be a valid Sanity API token with appropriate permissions for the actions being performed.

Action.description: Base schema for all actions. Every action must specify its type and any required parameters for that specific action type.

actionType.description:
The type of action to perform. This determines what other parameters are required and how the action will be processed.
The actionType must be one of the predefined values that correspond to the available actions in the API.

allOf.description: Creates a new document in the dataset.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a document creation action.

publishedId.description: The ID of the published document. This should be the full document ID without any prefixes.

ifExists.description: What to do if the document already exists.

document.description: The document to create. Must include `_type` and `_id` fields.

_id.description: The document ID. Note that document["_id"] must have either drafts. or versions.<release>. as a prefix and the portion following that prefix must be equal to publishedId.

allOf.description: Deletes a published document, and optionally its drafts and versions. The request fails with `409 Conflict` if any draft or version of the document exists that isn't listed in `includeDrafts`.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a document deletion action

publishedId.description: The ID of the document to delete. This should be the full document ID without any prefixes.

includeDrafts.description: An array of draft or version document IDs to delete alongside the published document. Each ID must be the `publishedId` with a `drafts.` or `versions.<release>.` prefix. Before API version `v2025-02-19`, only a single `drafts.` ID is allowed.

purge.description: If true, the document history is also deleted. This cannot be undone. Requires the `editHistory` permission, which no default role grants; you need a custom role.

allOf.description: An edit action is used to modify an existing document. It applies the given patch to the document referenced by versionId. If there is no such document then one is created using the current state of the published version and then that is updated accordingly.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a document edit action

publishedId.description: The ID of the document to edit. This should be the full document ID without any prefixes.

versionId.description: The ID of the version (or draft) to edit. This should be the full version ID.

patch.description:
The patch to apply to the document. Unlike a Mutations API patch, it has no `id` field; the target is `versionId`. Supported operations:
- set: Set a field to a value
- setIfMissing: Set a field only if it isn't already present
- unset: Remove a field
- insert: Insert items into an array, before or after a position, or replace items
- inc: Increment a number
- dec: Decrement a number
- diffMatchPatch: Apply a diff-match-patch to a string

See the [patch documentation](https://www.sanity.io/docs/content-lake/http-patches) for more on patches.

allOf.description: Publishes a draft or version document: its content replaces the published document, and the draft or version is deleted. The document referenced by `versionId` must exist.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a document publish action

publishedId.description: The ID of the document to publish. If the document is an existing draft or version, omit the `drafts.` or `versions.` prefix.

draftId.description:
The ID of the draft to publish. This should be the full draft ID including the 'drafts.' prefix. 
This parameter is deprecated. Use versionId instead.

versionId.description: The ID of the draft or version to publish. This should be the full ID including the `drafts.` or `versions.<release>.` prefix.

ifVersionRevisionId.description: The expected revision of the draft or version being published. Used to optimistically lock it so it isn't changed during publishing. Fails with `409 Conflict` if the revision doesn't match. Can't be combined with `ifDraftRevisionId`.

ifDraftRevisionId.description:
The expected revision of the draft being published.
This parameter is deprecated. Use ifVersionRevisionId instead.

ifPublishedRevisionId.description: The expected revision of the published document. Used to optimistically lock the published document so it isn't changed by other means during publishing. Fails with `409 Conflict` if the revision doesn't match.

allOf.description: Unpublishes a document by deleting the published document. If the document referenced by `versionId` doesn't exist, it's first created with the published content, so the content isn't lost.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a document unpublish action

publishedId.description:
The ID of the document to unpublish. This should be the full document ID without any prefixes.
The published document must exist.

versionId.description: The ID of the draft or version that keeps the content after unpublishing. This should be the full ID including the `drafts.` or `versions.<release>.` prefix.

allOf.description:
[DEPRECATED] Discards a document. Use version actions instead.
Deletes the draft of a document. It is an error if it does not exist.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a document discard action

draftId.description: The ID of the draft to discard, including the `drafts.` prefix. From API version `v2025-02-19`, a `versions.<release>.` ID is also accepted.

purge.description: If true, the document history is also deleted. This cannot be undone. Requires the `editHistory` permission, which no default role grants; you need a custom role.

allOf.description:
[DEPRECATED] Replaces a draft document. Use version actions instead.
Replaces the draft version of a document with the provided content.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a document replace draft action

publishedId.description: The ID of the published document whose draft is being replaced. This should be the full document ID without any prefixes.

attributes.description:
The document to replace the draft with. Must include `_id` and `_type` fields.
The `_id` must start with 'drafts.'.

_id.description: The document ID. Must start with 'drafts.'.

_type.description: The document type. Must match a schema type defined in your project.

allOf.description:
Creates a new version of a document in a release. Can either create from a complete document
or copy from an existing document with specified attributes.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a version creation action

publishedId.description: The ID of the published document to create a version of. This should be the full document ID without any prefixes.

document.description:
The document to create as a version. Must include `_id` and `_type` fields.
The `_id` must start with 'versions.<release>.' where <release> is the ID of the release.
If not provided, you must specify versionId and baseId to copy from an existing document.
Can't be combined with versionId, baseId, or ifBaseRevisionId.

_id.description: The document ID. Must start with 'versions.<release>.' where <release> is the ID of the release.

versionId.description:
The document ID to be created. Required when document is not provided.
Must start with 'versions.<release>.' where <release> is the ID of the release.

baseId.description: The ID of an existing document to copy attributes from. Required when document is not provided.

ifBaseRevisionId.description: Optional revision ID check for the document referenced by baseId. The action fails with `409 Conflict` if this does not match its current revision.

allOf.description: Discards a draft or version of a document. If purge is true, the document history is also deleted. Published documents can't be discarded.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a version discard action

versionId.description: The ID of the draft or version to discard. This should be the full ID including the `drafts.` or `versions.<release>.` prefix.

purge.description: If true, the document history is also deleted. This cannot be undone. Requires the `editHistory` permission, which no default role grants; you need a custom role.

allOf.description: Replaces the content of a draft or version of a document, creating it if needed. The document ID must start with either 'drafts.' or 'versions.<release>.'. Fails with `404 Not Found` if neither that draft or version nor the published document exists.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a version replace action

document.description:
The document to replace the existing version with. Must include `_id` and `_type` fields.
The `_id` must start with either 'drafts.' or 'versions.<release>.'.

_id.description: The document ID. Must start with either 'drafts.' or 'versions.<release>.'.

allOf.description: Marks a version for unpublishing. When the release is published, the published document will be removed.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a version unpublish action

versionId.description: The ID of the version to unpublish. This should be the full version ID including the 'versions.<release>.' prefix.

publishedId.description:
The ID of the published document to remove. This should be the full document ID without any prefixes.
The published document must exist.

allOf.description: Creates a new release in the `active` state. Fails with `409 Conflict` if a release with the same releaseId already exists, including published and archived releases that haven't been deleted.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release creation action

releaseId.description: The unique ID for the release. Can't match the ID of an existing release, including published and archived releases. Once a release is deleted, its ID can be reused.

metadata.description:
Optional metadata for the release. Can include title, description, and scheduling information.
Metadata is free-form: the API stores it as provided and doesn't validate these properties. The properties below are the ones Sanity Studio reads.

title.description: A human-readable title for the release

description.description: A detailed description of the release

releaseType.description:
The type of release, as used by Sanity Studio:
- asap: Release will be published as soon as possible
- undecided: Release timing is not yet determined
- scheduled: Release will be published at a specific time

intendedPublishAt.description:
The intended publish time for scheduled releases.
Only used when releaseType is 'scheduled'.

metadata.title: Spring 2024 Release
metadata.description: New features and improvements for spring

allOf.description: Modifies the metadata of an existing release. Only simple JSONMatch paths starting with 'metadata' are accepted, such as `metadata.title`.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release edit action

releaseId.description: The ID of the release to edit. The release must exist and not be published.

patch.description:
The patch to apply to the release metadata. Every path must start with 'metadata'.
Can include operations like set, unset, etc. Setting `metadata` itself replaces the whole metadata object, so target individual properties to keep the others.

ifRevisionID.description: Optional revision ID check for the release. The action fails with `409 Conflict` if this does not match the current revision of the release. Note the uppercase `ID`.

set.metadata.title: Updated Spring 2024 Release
set.metadata.description: Updated features and improvements for spring

allOf.description: Publishes all documents in a release. The release must be in the `active` state; to publish a scheduled release now, unschedule it first. Publishing runs asynchronously, so for larger releases the effect may take some time to be fully visible.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release publish action

releaseId.description: The ID of the release to publish. The release must exist and be in the `active` state.

ifRevisionID.description: Optional revision ID check for the release. The action fails with `409 Conflict` if this does not match the current revision of the release. Note the uppercase `ID`.

allOf.description: Archives a release, removing it from active releases. The documents remain in retention and can be accessed via history.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release archive action

releaseId.description: The ID of the release to archive. The release must exist and be in the `active` state.

ifRevisionID.description: Optional revision ID check for the release. The action fails with `409 Conflict` if this does not match the current revision of the release. Note the uppercase `ID`.

allOf.description: Restores an archived release and all its documents to their state before archiving.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release unarchive action

releaseId.description: The ID of the release to unarchive. The release must exist and be archived.

ifRevisionID.description: Optional revision ID check for the release. The action fails with `409 Conflict` if this does not match the current revision of the release. Note the uppercase `ID`.

allOf.description: Schedules a release for publishing at a future time. The release must be in the `active` state. Its documents are locked until it's published or unscheduled.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release schedule action

releaseId.description: The ID of the release to schedule. The release must exist and be in the `active` state.

publishAt.description: The time to publish the release. A time in the past isn't rejected; the release is published right away.

ifRevisionID.description: Optional revision ID check for the release. The action fails with `409 Conflict` if this does not match the current revision of the release. Note the uppercase `ID`.

allOf.description: Cancels a scheduled release. The release is unlocked and can be edited again.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release unschedule action

releaseId.description: The ID of the release to unschedule. The release must exist and be scheduled.

ifRevisionID.description: Optional revision ID check for the release. The action fails with `409 Conflict` if this does not match the current revision of the release. Note the uppercase `ID`.

allOf.description: Deletes a published or archived release. The backing system document will be removed from the dataset, and the releaseId can be reused. Fails if the release still contains documents.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release delete action

releaseId.description: The ID of the release to delete. The release must exist and be either published or archived.

ifRevisionID.description: Optional revision ID check for the release. The action fails with `409 Conflict` if this does not match the current revision of the release. Note the uppercase `ID`.

allOf.description:
Imports a release to a dataset. Used by the dataset import CLI to ensure releases are imported into a dataset.
Imported releases in the `scheduling` or `scheduled` state are reset to `active`. Importing a published or archived release deletes any leftover version documents for that release in the target dataset.

actionType.description: Identifies this as a release import action

releaseId.description: The ID of the release to import.

_id.description: The document ID. Must start with '_.releases.'.

name.description: The release name. Must match releaseId and the suffix of `_id`.

ifExists.description: What to do if the release already exists: fail with `409 Conflict`, leave the existing release unchanged, or replace it.

ActionsRequest.description:
A request containing one or more actions to be executed in a single transaction.
All actions must be valid and you must have permission to perform them.

actions.description:
An array of actions to execute. Each action must specify its type and required parameters.
Actions are executed in the order they appear in the array.

dryRun.description: If true, the actions will be executed but the results will not be saved.

skipCrossDatasetReferenceValidation.description: If true then any cross-dataset references will be considered weak for the purposes of this request.

transactionId.description: By default every transaction gets a random ID. This is included in Listener mutation events and the History API. This parameter lets you set your own transaction ID. It must be unique in the dataset; reusing an ID fails with `409 Conflict`.

visibility.description: Works like visibility field on Mutations API. It can be: sync, async or deferred. If sync the request will not return until the requested changes are visible to subsequent queries, if async the request will return immediately when the changes have been committed, but it might still be a second or so until you can see the change reflected in a query. For maximum performance, use async always, except when you need your next query to see the changes you made. deferred is the fastest way to write. It bypasses the real time indexing completely, and should be used in cases where you are bulk importing/mutating a large number of documents and don't need to see that data in a query for several tens of seconds.

ActionsResponse.description:
The response from a successful request. Actions are applied in a single transaction: either all of them succeed and the response is `200 OK`, or none of them are applied and an error response is returned.
Any warnings, such as deprecation notices, are returned in `X-Sanity-Warning` response headers.

transactionId.description: The ID of the transaction that applied the actions. It appears in Listener mutation events and the History API.
